trigger 601 clocks = 10.0167 us, pinned as an equality; 199 / 999 / 343 / 1375 mm
the trigger: 601 clocks, pinned as an equality
The device asks for 10 us MINIMUM, so the extra 17 ns is
harmless to a real sensor - and the check is an EQUALITY
anyway, because the act claims the COUNT and not a
datasheet floor. That is the same discipline
firmware/ws2812.pe uses when a 74-clock cell clears
SR_TRIG = 0x40 the PIN BIT - which pad drives the trigger
SR_TRIG_LEN = 149 the DELAY COUNT - how long it is held
SR_ECHO = 0x20 the echo pin bit, released and read back
Both SR_TRIG and SR_TRIG_LEN exist in peasm's CONSTS, which is
exactly why naming the wrong one is easy.

EXPECTED 1375 mm, and nothing was truncated.
8 000 = 64 * 125, so r = 0 and floor() is the identity.
AND THAT MAKES IT BLIND TO THE SMALL TERM, NOT SHARPER FOR IT
opposite of what an earlier revision of this figure claimed. With the small
term forced to 0: 1160 -> 198 WRONG, 5816 -> 990 WRONG, 2000 -> 341 WRONG,
and 8000 still -> 1375. The small term contributes 1, 9, 2 and
So run 3 does not test the small term at all - it ISOLATES 11*Q,
that is what earns it its place. Two further reasons, and both are the
OPPOSITE direction to blindness - they are where this run is SHARP:
the conversion masks the high byte of us with 0x3F, and those high bytes
slip in that mask (mutation sr-q-mask) is invisible in three runs and
caught only here: Q falls 125 -> 93, the answer 1375 -> 1023.

AND NOTE WHAT IS NOT IN THE TABLE.
No row is a failure, and no row is a
tolerance. The one number that could have been a band - the 11/64 constant's own
0.22 % against the speed of sound - is deliberately NOT here: it belongs to the
constant and not to the arithmetic, and folding it into a measured row would make
two different claims look like one number.
"387 WORDS VS 1024 REQUESTED" READS AS A DEFECT AND IS NOT ONE.
the imem is 1 024 words (IMEM_WORDS in the TB, pe_soc.v);
tools/fw/peasm.py pads the image to the requested width with 0xF000
is NOP, and says so in the generated file's own comment;
$readmemh into [0:1023] from a 387-word file leaves 637 words unwritten
and reports it only in a WARNING - so the testbench now counts the file's own
length, asks $readmemh for exactly that many words, and pre-fills the array with
, so the fill is a no-op region behind a
The earlier symptom-only narration - an image that looked short - was a consequence
of the testbench asking $readmemh for more words than the file held. The length is
counted now, which is why the number is PRINTED rather than inferred from a warning.
what this figure used to claim, and why the correction moved with the page
An earlier revision of this figure quoted the act's failing output verbatim, the way
a page quoting a defect has to:
and wiki/concepts/protocol-sr04.md carried the same quotation with a SIC marker,
tools/diag/delay_lattice.py carried a SIC EXEMPTION justified by it
Those had to move TOGETHER, and they did.
the marker is a self-limiting exemption by construction. A
marker on a conversion that now recomputes CORRECTLY is itself reported as a
finding, and a marker on a line with no conversion is reported as noise. So the
moment the quoted defect was fixed upstream, the marker's justification expired with
it - and a marker outliving the defect it marked would have switched off a real
check on a line that had become correct.
AND THE QUOTATION ITSELF HAD THREE ERRORS IN IT:
the derivation was +5 not +4, and the constant was SR_TRIG_LEN not SR_TRIG. The
unit error - 600 clocks reported as 10000.000 us, out by 1000 - was a fourth, and it was
fixed upstream in f7ac41b by adding CLK_US = CLK_NS / 1000.0.
The four targets are why the wrong derivation could not survive contact:
figure claiming 600 would be checked against a testbench that pins 601, and the
8 000 us run - the one with no truncation - is what makes the two senses of "exact"
separable on the page rather than a matter of opinion.
